mbm-1301.clue: I never skip the little ferry.
mbm-1301.quote: In my favorite adventure game you can jump straight across the river. I always pay the pixel ferryman anyway. My sister made him a paper tip jar to sit beside the controller.

mbm-1302.clue: I bow to the empty floor first.
mbm-1302.quote: At our martial-arts school the polished boards creak near the doorway. I practice my first turn there before class. If I can make the move without a creak, the rest of the room feels enormous.

mbm-1303.clue: I’m the person in the polished kettle.
mbm-1303.quote: I photographed my mother pouring tea and discovered my own tiny reflection in the kettle. I’ve kept that accidental self-portrait. It’s the only one of me wearing the whole kitchen ceiling as a hat.

mbm-1304.clue: I hemmed the music into my skirt.
mbm-1304.quote: I stitched three little notes from our favorite ballroom tune inside the hem. They don’t show when I stand still. My dance partner swears they appear on the quickest turn.

mbm-1305.clue: I let the wind pick our first throw.
mbm-1305.quote: We stand back to back with a single flying disc held overhead. Whoever feels the breeze first gets to throw downwind. On still days we wait long enough for the picnic sandwiches to come out.

mbm-1306.clue: I played a bottle of ink once.
mbm-1306.quote: In a children’s play I wore a purple barrel costume and tipped myself over when the poet sneezed. My blue-paper ink spread across the stage. Four children asked me to sign their programs with it.

mbm-1307.clue: I bought a postcard of the easy slope.
mbm-1307.quote: Everybody wanted a picture of the big mountain. I chose the little practice hill where my cousin first stood up on skis. If you squint at the postcard you can just see the yellow fence she held.

mbm-1308.clue: I made the river out of ribbons.
mbm-1308.quote: The map quilt I’m sewing uses blue gift ribbon from the parcels my mother used to mail. I twist it for rapids and smooth it out for the town bridge. Every parcel crossed a real river to reach me.

mbm-1309.clue: I stitched my cuff to my practice piece.
mbm-1309.quote: I was learning to sew buttonholes and caught my sleeve underneath. My friend freed me with two snips and made that scrap into a little badge. I wear it inside my sewing box.

mbm-1310.clue: I start a story with a smell.
mbm-1310.quote: I kept passing a shop that smelled of cedar. I wrote a detective who could find her way home by that smell alone. The shopkeeper likes the story and sends me wood curls in little envelopes.

mbm-1311.clue: I made a paper map of voices.
mbm-1311.quote: I stick a colored pin into the map for everyone I hear on the radio. One night the pins made a line almost straight across the water to a friend’s kitchen. She stuck a pin in her map for me.

mbm-1312.clue: I play the blue tee when the light is gold.
mbm-1312.quote: At the municipal course one tee has chipped blue paint. I like to start there in the evening because my shadow reaches halfway across it. For one quiet minute I feel thirteen feet tall.

mbm-1313.clue: I can set a ball by moonlight.
mbm-1313.quote: We stayed on the beach until the moon came up and the volleyball looked silver. Nobody kept score. We tried to keep the little silver moon in the air as long as possible.

mbm-1314.clue: I keep the tailor’s last sample.
mbm-1314.quote: When our neighborhood tailor retired he handed me his book of suit fabrics. I made him a quilt from the little squares. He can point to the cloth belonging to half the families on our street.

mbm-1315.clue: I put a bookmark on the butter dish.
mbm-1315.quote: I shaped a ceramic butter lid like a closed blue book. It has a little red clay ribbon down one edge. Visitors keep trying to read it before I tell them they can open it for toast.

mbm-1316.clue: I know which tent peg gets cold first.
mbm-1316.quote: On our last campout frost clung to the metal pegs before it touched the grass. I drew the little white stars around them in my notebook, then put the kettle on before anybody else woke.

mbm-1317.clue: I let the clock take the quiet seat.
mbm-1317.quote: Our park table wobbles under the chess clock. I put it on my folded newspaper to keep it from dancing away. The sports page earned a very tense draw on Tuesday.

mbm-1318.clue: I took my lunch on a little cruise.
mbm-1318.quote: We tied our raft to the bank and floated our peeled oranges in a bowl of cold river water. One orange escaped and made a magnificent first run through a tiny rapid. I got a wet sleeve rescuing it.

mbm-1319.clue: I remember the rope by the red fleck.
mbm-1319.quote: The bell tower has one rope with a tiny red thread among the blue. I reached for it during my first change and found my place without looking up. I put a red stitch in my practice notebook that night.

mbm-1320.clue: I made a key chain for an empty hook.
mbm-1320.quote: Our workshop has one hook where my grandfather’s keys used to hang. I beaded a little sunrise and hung it there. Light catches the orange beads just when his old shift used to begin.

mbm-1321.clue: I keep the mantel clock at quarter past four.
mbm-1321.quote: I’m making a quilt of the station where my parents met. Mum set the mantel clock to quarter past four so I could copy it. Dad laid her green scarf across the quilt to show me the color for his patch.

mbm-1322.clue: I made a handle from a question mark.
mbm-1322.quote: The clay curl I rolled for my mug looked just like a question mark. I added a dot of glaze beneath it. The mug comes out whenever my sister arrives with a difficult crossword.

mbm-1323.quote: My detective found a page torn from a recipe book. I wrote the recipe and physically tucked it between two chapters. I can swap the secret ingredient without rewriting the whole mystery.

mbm-1324.clue: I stopped playing for a ladybug.
mbm-1324.quote: A ladybug climbed onto the bridge at our mini-golf course and blocked my shot. We made it a tiny detour sign from a score pencil. By the time it flew off, half the queue was rooting for the bug.

mbm-1325.clue: I sew a pillow after every season.
mbm-1325.quote: My brother and I watch the space serial in pajamas. I stitched the outline of its rocket onto our oldest cushion. After each season we add one more little window with a new passenger inside.
